notes: Behavioral evals for the safaii-html markup conventions. Each targets a place a generic agent would default the wrong way: a div+role instead of a native element, a button-vs-link mixup, a zoom-blocking viewport, an unlabeled input, literal all-caps text, an unconditional opacity:0 reveal, or sloppy formatting. Run a fresh agent that reads SKILL.md (not the evals) per prompt, then grade the output against the expectations.

evals.prompt: I need a 'Sign up' button that opens a sign-up modal dialog. Give me the HTML, plus minimal JS if it's needed.
evals.expected_output: Native <dialog> opened with .showModal(); trigger and close are <button>s. No <div role="dialog">, no focus-trap library, no role="button", no re-added ARIA the native elements already provide.
expectations: Uses a native <dialog> element, not <div role="dialog">
Opens the dialog declaratively via command="show-modal"/commandfor (preferred) or via element.showModal() — either way it's the native dialog, getting focus trap / Escape / backdrop / inert free
Trigger and close controls are <button> elements, not <div>/<a> with role or onclick hacks
No focus-trap library or manual focus-management JS
Does not re-add ARIA roles the native <dialog>/<button> already provide

evals.prompt: On this page I need a 'Delete account' control and a 'Back to home' control. Mark them up.
evals.expected_output: Navigation ('Back to home') is an <a href="/">; the action ('Delete account') is a <button>. No <a href="#"> wired to JS, no <div>/<span> onclick.
expectations: The navigation control (Back to home) is an <a href>, not a button or a JS click handler
The action control (Delete account) is a <button>, not <a href="#"> + JS or a div/span onclick
No <a href="#"> used as a fake button
No <div>/<span> with onclick used as a control

evals.prompt: Give me the starting HTML shell for a new page titled 'About'.
evals.expected_output: <!doctype html>, <html lang>, <meta charset> first in head, a viewport that does NOT disable zoom, a descriptive page-specific <title>, and a <meta name="description">.
expectations: Includes <!doctype html> and lang on <html>
<meta charset="utf-8"> is present and first in <head>
viewport meta is present and does NOT disable zoom (no maximum-scale, no user-scalable=no)
A descriptive, page-specific <title> (e.g. mentions About)
Includes a <meta name="description">

evals.prompt: Build a newsletter signup form: an email field and a subscribe button.
evals.expected_output: <form action> with a labeled <input type="email" required autocomplete="email"> and a <button type="submit">. Native validation, real submission (not fetch), label not placeholder.
expectations: The email input has an associated <label> (for/id or wrapping the input)
Uses <input type="email"> with native validation (required), not a bare text input validated by JS
Submits via <button type="submit"> inside a <form action>, not a JS fetch handler
Includes a relevant autocomplete attribute (e.g. autocomplete="email")
Does not use a placeholder as a substitute for a label

evals.prompt: I want a submit button that displays in all caps: SUBMIT.
evals.expected_output: Markup text is 'Submit' (normal case); the all-caps look comes from CSS text-transform: uppercase. A <button> element. Literal all-caps text is avoided so screen readers don't spell it out.
expectations: The button's HTML text content is NOT literal all-caps — written as 'Submit', not 'SUBMIT'
All-caps appearance is achieved with CSS text-transform: uppercase
Uses a <button> element

evals.prompt: Fade my page sections in as they scroll into view.
evals.expected_output: js-ready (or similar) gate so the hidden state only applies when JS is present; IntersectionObserver triggers the reveal; opacity:0 hidden state sits inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference). Content stays visible without JS and isn't announced early.
expectations: The pre-reveal hidden state is gated so content stays visible without JS (e.g. only under a .js-ready / js-added root class)
Uses IntersectionObserver to trigger the reveal on scroll (not a scroll listener that reveals/announces early)
The hidden opacity:0 state is inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)
Does not set opacity:0 unconditionally (which hides content for no-JS users and still announces it to screen readers)

evals.prompt: Mark up a site header: a logo and a primary navigation menu of links.
evals.expected_output: <header> containing the logo and a <nav> whose links are in a <ul>. No role="banner"/role="navigation" repetition, no <div class="header">/<div class="nav">, no role="menu"/menuitem (those are for app menus, not site links).
expectations: Uses <header> and <nav> landmarks, not <div class="header"> / <div class="nav">
Does NOT add redundant role="navigation" or role="banner"
Navigation links are in a list (<ul><li><a>)
Does not use role="menu"/menuitem/aria-haspopup for plain site-navigation links

evals.prompt: Wire up a 'Sign up' button that opens a sign-up dialog, plus a button inside the dialog that closes it. Use the modern declarative approach, and make sure it still works in browsers that don't support it yet.
evals.expected_output: Open button: command="show-modal" commandfor="<dialog id>". Close button (inside the dialog): command="close" commandfor="<dialog id>". Native <dialog>, no onclick / addEventListener as the primary wiring. Plus a removable feature-detect fallback (e.g. checks 'commandForElement' in HTMLButtonElement.prototype) that calls .showModal()/.close() for pre-2025 browsers, marked as deletable later.
expectations: Open button uses command="show-modal" with commandfor pointing at the dialog's id
Close button (inside the dialog) uses command="close" with commandfor
Uses a native <dialog> element (no <div role="dialog">, no focus-trap library)
The declarative command/commandfor attributes are the PRIMARY wiring — not onclick / addEventListener
Includes a feature-detection fallback that wires .showModal()/.close() for browsers without invoker-command support
The fallback is marked as removable/temporary (a comment), not presented as a permanent solution

evals.prompt: I have an ordered list of steps, and I want them numbered with a custom style — and where a step has sub-steps, number those too (like 1, 1.1, 1.2, 2).
evals.expected_output: Native <ol> (nested <ol> for sub-steps) so the ordering is real and announced. Custom marker styling via @counter-style / list-style-type / ::marker keeps it accessible. If it uses counters()/counter() for the nested 1.1 display, it notes the generated-content screen-reader caveat and keeps the meaningful numbering in the native <ol> structure — NOT list-style:none + counters as the sole carrier of order.
expectations: Uses a native <ol> (with nested <ol> for sub-steps) — order is real markup, not faked with <div>/<ul>+counters
Custom numbering style is applied via list-style-type / @counter-style / ::marker, or counters() — not by abandoning the <ol> semantics
If counter()/counters() generated content is used for the 1.1 display, flags that generated content isn't reliably read by screen readers
Does NOT strip the list to list-style:none + CSS counters as the only source of the (meaningful) numbering
Keeps the meaningful order/number conveyed semantically (native <ol>), with CSS counters as presentation only

evals.prompt: I have a comment textarea that should grow to fit what the user types instead of staying a fixed height.
evals.expected_output: CSS field-sizing: content on the native <textarea> (with a <label>), bounded by min/max — NOT a JS auto-grow script. Light ask-first heads-up (Baseline 2026 June, degrades to fixed sizing).
expectations: Uses CSS field-sizing: content on the textarea — not a JS input-event auto-grow script
Bounds growth with min/max (e.g. max-height) rather than a fixed height
Native <textarea> with an associated <label>
Gives a light ask-first heads-up (Baseline 2026, graceful — degrades to normal fixed sizing)
Does not set a fixed height/width that would override field-sizing

evals.prompt: Make my <details> accordion smoothly expand and fade in when opened, instead of snapping open.
evals.expected_output: Animate the native <details> with the ::details-content pseudo-element: opacity + content-visibility ... allow-discrete for the fade, and interpolate-size: allow-keywords + height to auto for the expand (flagged Chromium-only enhancement). Whole thing gated under prefers-reduced-motion. No JS toggle / no height-measuring script.
expectations: Animates via the ::details-content pseudo-element (targets the open panel), not a JS height/measure script
Transitions content-visibility with allow-discrete so the fade survives collapse
For the height expand, uses interpolate-size: allow-keywords (animating to auto) and flags it as Chromium-only / progressive enhancement
Gates the whole animation under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)
Keeps the native <details>/<summary> (no JS toggle) and treats the motion as functional/subtle
Does not reach for a JS animation library or manual height measurement

evals.prompt: I want my sections to fade in as the user scrolls down to them.
evals.expected_output: The house safe-fade-in: js-ready gate + IntersectionObserver, hidden state under .js-ready and prefers-reduced-motion. NOT scroll-driven CSS animations (animation-timeline). If animation-timeline is mentioned, note it's not Baseline (no Safari) / decorative and prefer the safe-fade-in.
expectations: Reaches for the safe-fade-in pattern (js-ready gate + IntersectionObserver) — the house reveal pattern
Does NOT reach for scroll-driven CSS animations (animation-timeline: scroll()/view()) as the answer
If it mentions animation-timeline at all, flags it's not Baseline (no Safari) / decorative and prefers the safe-fade-in
Pre-reveal hidden state is gated (.js-ready + prefers-reduced-motion) so content stays visible without JS
Does not set opacity:0 unconditionally

evals.prompt: Style my form so invalid required fields show a red border — but I don't want fields flagged red before the user has even typed anything.
evals.expected_output: Use :user-invalid (and :user-valid for the success state) — NOT :invalid/:valid, which flag on load before interaction. Native validation (required), no JS. The :user-* selectors only match after the user interacts or tries to submit.
expectations: Uses :user-invalid (and/or :user-valid) for the validation styling
Does NOT use :invalid/:valid as the primary styling hook (they flag untouched fields on load)
Relies on native constraint validation (required, type=...), not a JS validation script
Notes or relies on :user-* matching only after interaction, so untouched required fields aren't flagged

evals.prompt: I have an off-canvas mobile nav that slides in. When it's closed/off-screen, make sure keyboard and screen-reader users can't tab into it.
evals.expected_output: Put the inert attribute on the off-canvas nav while it's closed (remove it when open) — that takes the subtree out of tab order, the a11y tree, and find-in-page in one attribute. NOT hand-rolled tabindex=-1 on every child or aria-hidden juggling.
expectations: Uses the inert attribute on the off-canvas nav while closed (toggled off when open)
Does NOT hand-roll tabindex="-1" on each focusable child or aria-hidden as the mechanism
Relies on inert removing the subtree from tab order + accessibility tree + find-in-page
Keeps it a real nav (native elements), toggling inert rather than rebuilding focus management in JS

evals.prompt: Mark up the site search box in my header — a search input and a button.
evals.expected_output: A <search> landmark wrapping a <form action> with a <label>, <input type="search">, and <button type="submit">. No role="search" on a div/form — the native <search> element provides the landmark.
expectations: Wraps the search form in a native <search> element (the search landmark)
Does NOT use role="search" on a <div>/<form> — uses the native element instead
Uses <input type="search"> with an associated <label>, inside a <form action>
Submit is a <button type="submit"> (real form submission)

evals.prompt: I have a long FAQ. Each answer is collapsed by default with a custom show/hide (not a <details>), but I still want answers to be found by the browser's Find-in-page.
evals.expected_output: Hide the collapsed answers with hidden="until-found" (not display:none) so find-in-page can discover and auto-reveal them. Ideally note that a native <details> is already findable, so it's the simpler choice if the design allows — hidden=until-found is for the custom case described.
expectations: Hides the collapsed answers with hidden="until-found" rather than display:none / the plain hidden attribute
Relies on find-in-page discovering + auto-revealing the content (beforematch), not a JS search index
Notes that native <details> is already find-in-page-friendly and is the simpler option when the design permits
Does not put hidden="until-found" on a display:none/contents/inline element (it needs a box to reveal)

evals.prompt: I have a close button that's just an X icon (an inline SVG, no text). Make it accessible.
evals.expected_output: Give the button an accessible name via aria-label ("Close") OR a visually-hidden .sr-only text span — NOT the title attribute, and never nameless. Hide the decorative SVG from assistive tech (aria-hidden="true"). If using .sr-only, use the canonical clip-path:inset(50%) recipe, not display:none.
expectations: Gives the icon-only <button> an accessible name via aria-label OR a visually-hidden .sr-only text span
Does NOT use the title attribute as the accessible name
Does NOT leave the button without an accessible name
Marks the decorative SVG aria-hidden="true" (or focusable="false") since the button carries the name
If it uses .sr-only, uses the canonical visually-hidden recipe (clip-path: inset(50%), 1px, overflow hidden) — not display:none/visibility:hidden

evals.prompt: I have a 'Role' text field where I want to suggest common roles (Designer, Developer, Manager) but still let people type their own.
evals.expected_output: A native <input list="..."> wired to a <datalist> of <option>s (with a <label>) — suggestions that don't restrict free text. No custom JS autocomplete/dropdown. (A <select> would be wrong since it restricts to the listed values.)
expectations: Uses <input list="..."> wired to a <datalist> with <option> suggestions
Does NOT build a custom JS autocomplete / dropdown widget
Keeps the input free-text (datalist suggests, doesn't restrict) — matches 'type their own'
Has an associated <label>; native form control
Does not use a <select> (which would restrict to the listed roles)
